PSG: Why Doue's serious injury could derail Luis Enrique's season

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (917 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:48.
  • PSG's 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday at the Allianz Riviera, in round 11 of Ligue 1, brought terrible news for Luis Enrique.
  • Shortly before half-time, Desire Doue, who had scored a goal minutes earlier, collapsed to the ground after twisting his right knee while attempting a dribble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:48.

PSG's 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday at the Allianz Riviera, in round 11 of Ligue 1, brought terrible news for Luis Enrique.

Shortly before half-time, Desire Doue, who had scored a goal minutes earlier, collapsed to the ground after twisting his right knee while attempting a dribble. Amid cries of pain, the winger had to leave the pitch on a stretcher when substituted.

Speaking to Ligue 1+, the Spanish manager said in advance that Doue's injury 'was serious', a fear confirmed on Sunday. Imaging results found that the PSG number 14 has suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament and will have to undergo surgery in the coming days.

It has been revealed that PSG have not disclosed a recovery timeline, but cases similar to Desire Doue's that require surgical intervention show that players usually spend at least six months in the medical department. The 21-year-old Frenchman should therefore only return to action at the end of May.

According to recent reports, in the most optimistic scenario, Doue would be fit in time for a possible Champions League final, to be played on 5 June at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Spain. However, depending on the strategy PSG adopt to cover for the young winger's absence, the success of this season is at risk.

Signed in August 2024 from Rennes for £42.5m (€50m), Desire Doue became one of Luis Enrique's trusted men, so much so that he was an crucial part of the rotation in his debut season (16 goals and 14 assists in 61 matches) and was named man of the match in the European final against Inter Milan, when he scored twice.

Recent findings suggest that in 2025-26, the French attacking midfielder had his run at PSG interrupted by two muscle injuries, but still managed 13 goals and eight assists in 40 matches, as well as scoring his penalty as PSG won back-to-back Champions League titles against Arsenal. And after representing his country at the World Cup, Doue was enjoying an overwhelming start to the season.

As a reward for his good form at PSG, Doue began to gain more space in the France team under Zinedine Zidane, who even stated that he reminded him of himself when he played as a midfielder, because of his personality of always wanting to improve by listening to older players.

More than the impact in the final third, Doue is also a joker for the PSG manager because of his two-footedness, able to play on either wing.

The Frenchman had been playing on the left in recent weeks as a replacement for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who also suffered an anterior cruciate ligament rupture in his right knee during the win over Barcelona on 20 October, in the Champions League.

Industry observers note that the Georgian underwent surgery and should only be available to the Spanish manager in mid-April. With two heavyweight absences in the attacking system, PSG must ask themselves whether it is necessary to reinforce the area when the transfer window reopens, or whether the current squad will be enough to remain competitive on all fronts.

If PSG conclude that the solution lies in the market, they will have to do very meticulous work to find someone who fits Luis Enrique's playing philosophy, based on high intensity and constant movement, and who is available to leave in January. It is true that there is no shortage of talents around the world who fit those requirements, but the certainty is that no signing would be cheap, nor a guarantee of immediate success.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, if PSG give a vote of confidence to the current players, which at the moment is the public discourse, they will have to get more out of their players. 2025 Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele has suffered from different physical problems in 2026-27, so much so that he has constantly been placed on a load management regime.

Ferran Torres, signed from Barcelona for £42.5m (€50m), had an exciting start at PSG, with seven goals in the first six matches. However, as in his Camp Nou days, the Spanish forward began to fluctuate and went eight games without scoring, ending the drought against Nice.

In a recent development, maghnes Akliouche, bought from Monaco for £42.5m (€50m), has not yet reached his full potential (two goals and three assists in 16 matches), which is normal for a newcomer. But the lack of prior experience as a protagonist in the Champions League raises doubts over whether the 24-year-old Frenchman is able to make a difference for PSG.

It is a similar case to Mika Godts, acquired from Ajax for £46.8m (€55m), but with the aggravating factor that he is still going through the process of adapting to French football. As he is still 21, the Belgian winger has been inconsistent at PSG, with two goals and two assists in 12 matches.

Industry observers note that finally, Senny Mayulu (20) and Quentin Ndjantou (19) are academy gems still looking to establish themselves among the professionals. The Spanish manager does have the possibility of pushing Nuno Mendes and/or Achraf Hakimi forward, but that would create a problem at full-back.

PSG have seven more games until the winter break, but with Ligue 1, the Coupe de France and the Intercontinental Cup, it is undeniable that the mission of chasing a third successive Champions League title has become much harder without Doue.

Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.
  • Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five.
  • But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that “The data is not crucial,” Alonso remarked. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”.

In a recent development, chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

Recent findings suggest that “After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso stated. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”.

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

In a recent development, alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl.

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez stated. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was swiftly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

According to recent reports, “We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”.

Chelsea’s latest set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Industry observers note that macPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Industry observers note that fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, stated his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”.

According to recent reports, palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro claims he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert.

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup will be hosted jointly by England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, FIFA have confirmed, with the tournament returning to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966.

The UK was the sole bidder to host the tournament, and received a 4.3 out of 5 rating from FIFA evaluators.

Industry observers note that the bid has put forward 19 potential venues, including five in London: Wembley Stadium, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Emirates, Stamford Bridge and a renovated Selhurst Park. Old Trafford will be considered, regardless of whether Manchester United moves to its proposed latest home.

Some 32 teams will contest the 2027 World Cup in Brazil, but this is due to expand to 48 from 2031 onwards. The tournament, then, will comprise 104 matches.

Sources indicate that england has not hosted a major tournament since staging the women’s European Championships in 2022, which the Lionesses won. It has failed in bids to host the 2006 and 2018 men’s World Cups. England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the Men’s European Championship in 2028.

Sources indicate that it is understood that the process of finalising the list of stadia that will be used is ongoing and is under FIFA’s jurisdiction. Wembley is the only stadium that presently meets the standards required to host the World Cup final.

South East Water slumps to loss after hefty bill from supply failures.

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean.

It is still to be decided how many of the co-host nations will qualify automatically for the tournament.

According to recent reports, the 2035 World Cup bid has also put forward a host stadium in Northern Ireland - Belfast’s Windsor Park - and two each in Scotland and Wales. The Scottish grounds are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road, while the Welsh pair are both in Cardiff: the Millennium Stadium and the Cardiff City Stadium.

The remaining English host stadiums are: Villa Park, The AmEx, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, and the Stadium of Light.

According to recent reports, three more stadia could be added to the bid, most notably a potential newly introduced Chelsea ground. Discussions as to the future of Stamford Bridge have been bubbling away for decades as the club’s hierarchy debate whether to redevelop the current ground, knock it down to build a new one on the current site, or move to a new site altogether.

Birmingham City’s new Powerhouse Stadium and Wrexham’s renovated Racecourse Ground could also host matches.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed the news, saying: “The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

In a recent development, “Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.”.

FA CEO Mark Bullingham said: “Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.”.

England last hosted a World Cup in 1966, when the men’s team famously beat West Germany 4-2 in the final to seal the nation’s first major honour. The Lionesses have since become back-to-back Euros champions in 2022 and 2025, but suffered World Cup final heartbreak in 2023 when they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in Sydney.

Before the UK’s host bid for 2035 was confirmed at a special FIFA Congress, it was also revealed that a joint bid by the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica had been approved to host the 2031 World Cup.

Ruben Amorim is not a coach who makes a habit of singling out individuals, but he made an exception in Saturday’s press conference.

In a recent development, as MilanNews recall, on the eve of the game against Frosinone, Amorim bluntly admitted that Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot are the ‘irreplaceable’ players in the current squad. Their characteristics and their quality make them unique, in the eyes of the coach and many fans.

In a recent development, when the American and the Frenchman don’t play, the team’s fluidity and effectiveness suffer significantly. There is a stark contract between Milan when Rabiot and Pulisic play versus when both do not feature.

It has been revealed that amorim’s words were clear in his pre-match presser: “Every player appreciates having the club’s trust. And Pulisic’s new contract has helped. When he wasn’t playing, I told you he was still notable for Milan, and we can’t forget about the injured players.

“Pulisic is the only player we can’t replace today: the way he moves between the lines, we don’t have another Pulisic. In the last few European matches, we missed him; we had to manage him. If he’s not on the pitch, given his characteristics, you feel it.

“And you understand how key he is. He doesn’t talk much, but he speaks a lot on the pitch with his play. He always wants the ball. He and Rabiot always lift the team up. I don’t like to talk about individuals, but I have to.

“I think everyone can understand that. So Pulisic is our present, he will be our future, and I think he has the potential to do even more.”.

Sources indicate that it’s worth noting that the coach emphasised the importance of Pulisic’s contract renewal too. This is also why the club are doing everything possible to reach an agreement for Rabiot.

Cardinale called him a top player and candidly admitted that he adores him, also emphasising how he respects his family. These statements are not coincidental, given that it is his mother who represents the midfielder.

Speaking of which, discussions with Véronique Rabiot are progressing positively. A meeting took place before the derby, which ended with a 3-1 win with a goal for the former Juventus and Marseille midfielder.

Industry observers note that the player is happy with the Rossoneri and wants to stay: a definitive agreement on the financial terms needs to be reached. Milan are also willing to adjust the player’s salary in order to secure him for a few more years at Milanello.

Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone quipped, "You don't win 345 matches defending" after he broke the record for the most wins as a manager in LaLiga history.

Simeone levelled Luis Aragones' record on October 31, but after a loss to Barcelona before the international break, he had to wait for his record-breaking victory.

And he got it on Sunday, with Atletico brushing aside Getafe 3-0 with a confident performance.

Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso put Atletico 2-0 up by the half-hour mark, and Alejandro Grimaldo added some late gloss from the spot with a stoppage-time penalty.

It means that Simeone has now won 345 matches in LaLiga, officially surpassing Aragones in the standings, and doing so in 189 fewer games.

Simeone reached that total in 567 matches (also D123 L99), while Aragones tallied 344 wins in 756 outings.

Asked how he felt about breaking the record, Simeone remarked: "An enormous joy, I cannot deny it.

"A lot of work behind it, a lot of effort from many people, many players thrown into an idea.

"That constant criticism we always receive, which I don't value, but I keep observing it: that defensive phase they've already imposed on us, and it seems we always play defensively to defend.

Industry observers note that "You don't win 345 matches defending. Is it allowed?".

Overall, they have only lost one away game in LaLiga this season (a 3-0 loss to Athletic Club), and Simeone is thrilled with this particular strength.

Recent findings suggest that "We are interpreting away games better," he added. "Goals give you that calm to have continuity in the match.

Sources indicate that "We need to stay in the same direction. We came off a very good 55 minutes against Barca. The result was tough; it was hard for almost all the teams in Europe to compete again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on. The senior fixtures don’t start until Thursday, so we haven’t even got a fresh batch of international press conference quotes to sink our teeth into. Slim pickings.

According to recent reports, this time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally. All the more so when you consider Noni Madueke can count himself unlucky to have missed out for England, while Bukayo Saka and William Saliba would ordinarily be shoo-ins.

Any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2. More minutes in his legs, rather than another injury to worry about.

Bolstered by Saliba and Max Dowman, whose domestic suspension kept him out of Saturday’s game, the youngsters ran out 5-2 winners. Given they’re right now 21st out of 31 teams in their Swiss-style league table, perhaps this is the way forward. Send the substantial guns down a level and start battering our way towards more club silverware. Relentless madman Arteta, finding latest frontiers for his evil genius. He doesn’t just leave his technical area. He thinks outside it.

If you missed it, Max has been promoted to England’s under-21s for this window. He’ll join Arsenal loanees Tommy Setford and Ethan Nwaneri, as well as former Hale Enders Brooke Norton-Cuffy, who came off the bench for Hull on Saturday, and Amario Cozier-Duberry, who seems to be doing well at Middlesbrough on loan from Brighton.

In a recent development, given Max has been in and around Mikel Arteta’s first team for a couple of seasons now, it’s easy to take milestones like this for granted. But playing under-21 international football at 16 is another significant step, even for someone whose talent has made rapid progress seem almost routine.

According to recent reports, back in September, Lee Carsley described his eventual promotion as inevitable, while stressing that the timing had to be right. The point was to bring him into a squad where he could play and compete, rather than move him up simply because everyone expected it.

Carsley referenced Nwaneri when discussing the temptation to push exceptional youngsters through the age groups. His point was that the aim is a long senior career, not winning a race to the first cap. That seems sensible enough. Max doesn’t need every appearance to become an audition for the next level.

Recent findings suggest that A couple of games against Portugal and France should be a useful challenge in their own right. Carsley and Arteta also know each other from their Everton days, which ought to help when discussing what he needs.

Industry observers note that with England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland hosting Euro 2028, you can imagine that tournament already features somewhere in Max’s ambitions. There’s plenty of football between now and then, though. For the moment, let’s see how he gets on with this next step.

Elsewhere, most of our European internationals will be occupied with the Nations League, while the South American trio rack up the air miles again. Piero Hincapie heads home to Ecuador for friendlies against Costa Rica and Bolivia, while Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes face Japan and Singapore, both in Singapore.

According to recent reports, I appreciate Brazil’s options are more limited when European teams are tied up with UEFA fixtures, but their friendly schedule does sometimes feel like somebody has thrown a dart at a map. No doubt the commercial logic is compelling, but that doesn’t make you any less worried about tired hamstrings.

Anyway, fingers crossed they all come back with their limbs intact.

According to recent reports, in other news, Italian publication Tuttosport has named Andrea Berta the winner of its Best Executive Award at this year’s Golden Boy Awards. The Arsenal sporting director collects the gong three transfer windows into his tenure, the latest of which ended with some fans calling for his head after the failed pursuits of Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez.

In a recent development, either the bar is pretty low, he’s basking in the reflected glory of the team’s success, or it’s one of those shindigs where buying an inordinately expensive table guarantees you something shiny to take home. The cynic in me wasn’t exactly silenced by the news that Joan Laporta won Best President and Jorge Mendes Best Agent. In fact, I snorted when I read that. And lest we forget, Edu picked up a similar award from the same organisers in 2023….

Sources indicate that myles Lewis-Skelly was in contention for the actual Golden Boy award, which went to Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi. Hard to argue too much with that, given the 19-year-old was at the heart of Spain’s World Cup win.

Cubarsi also made the FIFPRO World 11. More pertinently for us, so did David Raya. Having finished second to compatriot Unai Simon in the Ballon d’Or’s Best Goalkeeper category, I imagine there’s some satisfaction in getting the nod from the people who actually play the game. More than 26,000 professionals from 75 countries cast their votes, which is a fairly substantial dressing room to win over.

Alessia Russo, who is in fine form even if Arsenal Women are not, also earned her third selection for the Women’s World 11.

As you’ll have gathered from the snippiness above, I find it easy to be cynical about these things. There are so many awards now that you half expect to get one for finding your seat at the ceremony. Still, sometimes it’s nice to give people a pat on the back and recognise a job well done.

Recent findings suggest that on an entirely unrelated note, have you voted for us to win Best Fan Media at the upcoming FSA Awards? You’ve only got a week left. A prestigious honour, that one. 😉.

In a recent development, right, I think that’s as much toothpaste as I can squeeze out of a slow news day. If anything else happens, we’ll have it covered on Arseblog News. Catch you next time.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester United's hierarchy have been accused of negligence by former captain Gary Neville after failing to strengthen their defence during the summer transfer window.
  • The Red Devils slumped to a concerning upcoming low as they suffered a humbling 4-0 defeat against rivals Liverpool on Sunday, leaving them 19th in the Premier League table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 11:22.

Manchester United's hierarchy have been accused of negligence by former captain Gary Neville after failing to strengthen their defence during the summer transfer window.

The Red Devils slumped to a concerning upcoming low as they suffered a humbling 4-0 defeat against rivals Liverpool on Sunday, leaving them 19th in the Premier League table.

Latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino became the first boss in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his opening match in charge of a club.

Liverpool took advantage of Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card and ran riot on Merseyside, with goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz condemning the Red Devils to their fifth league loss of the season.

Man United have posted only one win in 11 league games this season, while they have now conceded 34 goals across all competitions – the highest total of any team across Europe's top-five divisions.

Commenting on Man United’s defensive woes as a pundit for Sky Sports, Neville stated: "It's negligent. The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years.".

Man United instead opted to prioritise a midfield rebuild, with Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans all brought in for a combined fee in the region of £150m.

Pochettino’s nightmare start to life as Man United boss could not have gone much worse, and his decision to hand Matthias de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days has been called into question by Neville.

The Dutch defender, who recently recovered from a long-term injury, was partly at fault for the first goal conceded by the Red Devils, misjudging a high ball that led to Yoro’s red card, and he was run ragged by Liverpool’s pacey frontline all afternoon.

"[Myself and Jamie Carragher] were in the trucks over in the compound and when the team came through straight away we were very surprised," mentioned Neville.

"I just didn't think Manchester United would win, and I thought they would concede lots of goals and make mistakes. Maybe the options on the bench aren't brilliant either, but it's really desperate and it's tiring watching them.

Sources indicate that "Mauricio Pochettino's options are not great, but I didn't get De Ligt. Having been out for a year myself, it's really difficult to come back into a game like that.

It has been revealed that "I'm not saying that you can't, but as a centre-back getting your bearings… You saw him in Como (4-1 defeat in the Champions League), he was all over the place in Como. It's almost like you don't know what's happening.

According to recent reports, "I found that coming back into it when I was 32, he's obviously more experienced as well. I was very surprised he played but then the others haven't been doing great either.".

While Neville believes that a back four of Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw (currently injured) represents the “best” back four for Man United, playing with other defensive combinations will see the club get relegated.

"You wonder how low it can get, but this is as low as it's been in 54 years," Neville added. "A few weeks ago against Fulham, I noted it's the worst 40 minutes or 30 minutes I've seen in my lifetime.

It has been revealed that "At the time people said that was maybe a bit too much, but this is actually the worst Manchester United have ever been in 54 years. It's a fact. The worst defensive team in Europe, second bottom in the league, they've never started this badly.".

He continued: "I would have started with Harry Maguire today. Manchester United's best back four - and I think we're informed enough to know, we've watched these lads for two or three years - is [Luke] Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and Martinez.

It has been revealed that "Now, it's a poor back four, let me be really clear. But it is Manchester United's best back four.

"Now, if you can get that back four out on the pitch, it does win games, against Liverpool last year, it does win games against City and Arsenal, it can compete slightly.

"But that back four that started today, and the one that finished against Villa a few weeks ago of [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Patrick] Dorgu, Yoro, and [Ayden] Heaven - that will get you relegated, that's a fact.".

Man United’s total of just eight Premier League points after 11 matches is their lowest at this stage of a top-flight season since 1972-73, but Pochettino’s side are only one point adrift of safety heading into their next league fixture at home to Brentford on Saturday.

NFL icon Tom Brady has purchased a small stake in Premier League giants Chelsea, according to ESPN.

It would see the seven-time Super Bowl champion make a swift return to investment in English football after he stepped away from Championship leaders Birmingham City earlier this month.

Brady was in attendance at the MetLife Stadium in Latest Jersey when Chelsea beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the 2025 Club World Cup final.

The New England Patriots icon, who also owns a minority stake in the NFL's Las Vegas Raiders, reportedly has a good relationship with Behdad Eghbali, who oversees the club’s Clearlake Capital ownership.

Chelsea declined to comment when approached, but sources have stood up the negotiations.

In a recent development, brady, the greatest quarterback of all time, secured a minority stake in Birmingham in August 2023. That followed Tom Wagner purchasing a 45 percent stake at the club earlier that same year.

NFL icon Tom Brady has purchased a small stake in Premier League giants Chelsea.

Brady watched Chelsea beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the 2025 Club World Cup final.

At Birmingham, Brady made headlines when he questioned Wayne Rooney’s work ethic during a documentary following his time at St Andrew’s.

Rooney, who went on to be sacked after just 15 games in charge, later described those comments as ‘very unfair’.

In a recent development, when Brady exited Birmingham, the club mentioned in a statement: ‘Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years. It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.’.

Chelsea have invited minority shareholders with their women’s team.

NBA star Giannis Antetokounmpo previously purchased a stake in the side, partnering with Alexis Ohanian, the founder of social media platform Reddit who likewise invested in the team in 2025.

Zubimendi addresses tiredness and transfer talk

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1286 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Martin’s Day in Germany, a day I’d never heard of until I had a child over here.
  • Martin was, as the story goes, a 4th-Century Roman soldier and is best known for sharing his cloak with a freezing beggar.
  • In a recent development, fitting, then, that Martin Zubimendi should be linked with a move to Chelsea (and others).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Good morning all, hope you’re well! It’s St. Martin’s Day in Germany, a day I’d never heard of until I had a child over here. Kids will leave Kindergarten and chant as they walk through their neighbourhoods with lanterns this evening, as is tradition. Doesn’t sound creepy at all, does it?

It has been revealed that st. Martin was, as the story goes, a 4th-Century Roman soldier and is best known for sharing his cloak with a freezing beggar.

In a recent development, fitting, then, that Martin Zubimendi should be linked with a move to Chelsea (and others). It would be the saintly thing to do to share some of our midfield spoils with the desperate, downtrodden, shivering squad that Xabi Alonso has at his disposal. I hope we let them get absolutely glacial – Siberian, even, given their history – and keep our glorious cloak of midfielders all to ourselves.

The first rule of the international break is, of course, to ignore all transfer rumours. Club football goes away but there are still pages to fill, newspapers to sell, online traffic to amass, and something has to fill the void.

And, speaking to Marca, the midfielder has denied that he’s unhappy:.

I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. (Not playing) is something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very promptly.

Asked about the toll that playing so much took on him last season – Zubimendi was the only Arsenal player to play in all 38 Premier League games, he started 34 of those and had the third most minutes in the squad, behind David Raya and Declan Rice, across all competitions – he admitted that that was a factor:.

I don’t like to blame everything on my physical condition, but I definitely noticed it that year. It was a new year for me, with a lot of new stimuli. I played a huge number of minutes and, to be honest, I was tired. Then there were other things too, but one of them could very well have been my physical condition.

I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the blueprint to me. He warned me that there were upcoming signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

And he completely dismissed any suggestion that he is talking to other clubs, given those links to the Madrid sides and Chelsea:.

I haven’t wasted any energy on outside things. I’m busy enough trying to earn a place, get playing time, and fight to win this Premier League, which is looking so promising. I haven’t spent any energy on it, nor have I contacted anyone.

To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish. Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close (to a transfer), but not at all.

Sources indicate that still, I do think the case of Zubimendi is an interesting one. Having lost his place late last season, he returned late in the summer, and is yet to start a Premier League game in 2026-27 following the emergence of Myles Lewis-Skelly and the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes.

Here we have a player Arsenal desperately wanted and agreed a deal for a year ahead of signing him, would they really be looking to move him on again now that he’s spent what is essentially just a quarter of a season not as first choice? So much focus has been placed on building a squad that can sustain injuries or absences, and then we’d leave ourselves light again?

Industry observers note that maybe? You never can know how transfers pan out ahead of time, and things can change quickly in football but, as Zubimendi suggests, they can change quickly in the other direction again too. Did anyone, for instance, envisage Lewis-Skelly starting against Atletico Madrid just a week before it actually happened?

I do think his particular rise, and a stressful second half of the season, has clouded what we all thought of Zubimendi’s first half-season at Arsenal, and how much he contributed across the entire campaign. At this stage a year ago, we were two points worse off than we are now but still top of the league by six points, with more goals scored and fewer goals conceded than we are 10 games in this time around. He was a big part of that.

It has been revealed that he was a huge part of winning the title and reaching the Champions League final – he started 43 of our 53 games across those two competitions. He started every Champions League knockout game up until the semi-final second leg and played all of extra-time in the final.

And if he was suffering physically, there was no break in the summer, as he went off to the World Cup, Spain went all the way, and he was back on the pitch for Arsenal (having had no pre-season) in Cardiff as we won the Community Shield, less than a month on from the World Cup final.

For all that, I can also see why someone would possibly want to make the case for moving on. Seeing a player not be used (Zubimendi has played in seven of our league games so far this season, by the way!) feels like an obvious place to upgrade, and we’ve been scarred before by letting players sit on the bench before then struggling to move them on for a fair fee.

We’re also going to need to refresh the age of the team and especially the midfield before long. When you don’t just look at the players themselves but actually account for who is playing the minutes, we have the third-oldest squad in the league this season. The frontline will need fresh faces soon – that’s not news to anyone – in terms of age as well as quality, but the midfield will need it on the age front as well.

We’ve also given the fewest minutes in the league to players under the age of 23 (around 6%) by some distance. If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it, but if you don’t get the balance right it will break in time.

It has been revealed that right now, though, this season, we’re likely to need our whole squad. We can’t be making it weaker. If one of Declan Rice – God forbid – or Bruno Guimaraes were to pick up a knock and miss a month, Zubimendi would suddenly be in line for a lot of football. Zubimendi who, again, was central to us winning the league last season.

It’s far too soon into the season to write his campaign off, especially when we saw how things changed so suddenly in that exact position back in May. Let’s see how things look when the summer rolls around, but there’s no need to rush into a decision.

Recent findings suggest that right then, have a great day all – and I’ll leave you with the gorgeous generosity of another St. Martin close to our hearts.

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

Industry observers note that in the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “latest signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

In a recent development, man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

Recent findings suggest that when the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

It has been revealed that reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick remarked: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

Industry observers note that “So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”.

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder shows near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate–forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

Industry News: The virtues of patience

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1323 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it’s 13 December 2020.
  • According to recent reports, it was freezing and wet at the Emirates.
  • Recent findings suggest that willian was grotesquely slow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let’s take a journey back in time.

It has been revealed that it’s 13 December 2020. Arsenal versus Burnley.

According to recent reports, it was freezing and wet at the Emirates. Only 2,000 fans had been allowed in because of Covid, and my mum, my dad, my mate Ben and I made up four of them. We were socially distanced and wearing masks. My glasses kept steaming up.

This was supposed to be fun. Watching my team.

Recent findings suggest that willian was grotesquely slow. Alex Lacazette was profligate. Rob Holding was bald. Very bald. And Granit Xhaka was angry. So angry, in fact, that in the second half he put his hands around the throat of some opposition goon and, after a VAR review, got himself sent off. There were boos. As many as 2,000 people could muster, anyway.

Then our captain, Pierre Emerick-Aubameyang, headed a corner into his own net. You couldn’t make it up. Except you could. It was the only goal of the game.

By then the steam fogging up my specs might as well have been coming out of my ears. In his player ratings, Andrew M called Xhaka the ‘King of the Idiots’ and described the match and the result as ‘utterly shit’. Which was fair.

It was our seventh defeat in 10 league games and our fourth in a row at home, something that hadn’t happened since 1953. We were 15th, five points above the relegation zone.

And who was top? Sp*rs. Managed by everyone’s favourite sociopath, Jose Mourinho. Having beaten us in the North London derby the week before, they couldn’t stop gloating.

According to recent reports, I’d bought into the Arteta project hook, line and sinker. I still wanted him to be the right man for the job. I was just finding it harder to explain why I thought he was. The FA Cup win had been four months earlier. It felt like years.

The tree, to paraphrase our manager, was shaking.

It has been revealed that it had been shaking for a good two and a half years by then. The soggy bottom of the Arsene Wenger era had left its scars. Those two 3-0 defeats to City in the space of a week still make me wince. Then came the hope that Unai Emery might get us back on track. By the time we’d seen how that played out, I’d got into the habit of talking myself down whenever things looked up. Maybe we’ll get better. Give it time.

The trouble with rock bottom is you never know if there’s another floor below it. Was Burnley ours? I’m still writing about it six years later, so it was probably mine. There were games against Southampton and Everton before Christmas, and I can barely remember either of them.

Then came Boxing Day and a visit from Frank Lampard’s Chelsea. Is it reductive to say that was the day everything changed for Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal? Probably. But my word, watching Bukayo Saka, Emile Smith Rowe and Gabriel Martinelli tear about the place was the fix this addict needed. We went on an unbeaten run after that. Seven whole games! And for the first time in weeks, I was looking forward to what came next.

And here we are in November 2026. Reigning champions of England. Top of the league again. Five points clear. Odds-on favourites to retain the title after 10 games. Sure, throwing hundreds of millions of American dollars at the problem helped. But if there’s a lesson in all this, it’s that hard work and patience pay off.

Which is why I’m using today’s blog to appeal directly to Sir Jim Ratcliffe to give Michael Carrick a stay of execution.

According to recent reports, come on, man, you’re probably still paying off Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, maybe even Ralf Rangnick. Do you really want to go back to the drawing board all over again? Carrick is the man for the Manchester United hot seat. Just look at the way he wore a poppy-embroidered armband as well as a poppy badge at the weekend. The man doesn’t do half measures. He’s a two-scoops guy. Surely that’s something you, a multibillionaire British-born petrochemicals tycoon who lives in Monaco, can get on board with?

Sources indicate that I know Mauricio Pochettino might be tempting. He’s got floppy hair, a tan and, despite the Sp*rsy stench, has come to resemble a rather huggable teddy bear. But think it through, Jim. What if he comes in and everybody perks up? It’s much harder to make job cuts and to force out season ticket holders when people are enjoying themselves. Best get through that process first while Michael turns the oil tanker round. It’s not far off, promise, you’re on a two-game unbeaten streak!

Industry observers note that anyway, what would sacking Carrick say about patience? Look at Arteta. There were people who wanted him gone after Burnley and, as you’ve just read, I was close to joining them. Imagine if the club had listened to me. All those years of work, all that progress, all the joy I’ve had watching Arsenal lately. We could have thrown it all away because a man in a damp mask couldn’t see out of his glasses.

So give Carrick time. Give him January. Give him a full pre-season. And if things still haven’t picked up by this time next year, ask yourself whether one full pre-season, and £100 million on Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, was ever really enough.

I can only speak for myself, Jim, but I haven’t looked forward to watching Manchester United this much in years.

Right, let’s see if that works….

The Interlull kicks into gear tonight. David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi are in action for Spain against Czechia, Riccardo Calafiori’s Italy take on France, and England face Croatia at Wembley.

Ezri Konsa and Myles Lewis-Skelly will both miss out at Wembley. Konsa is working on his fitness but will be available to face Spain on Sunday, while our Hale Ender is suspended after picking up two bookings in the Nations League.

Elsewhere, ahead of Sweden’s game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, Viktor Gyokeres has been speaking to the press. Like Martin Zubimendi, he indicates he’s happy at Arsenal.

“I want to,” he mentioned, when asked if he’s keen to stay at the Emirates.

“It feels good when I’ve played. We’ve won most of the games. It was a tough loss in the cup (against Fleetwood). Otherwise it’s felt good for myself and the team, notes the forward. I’ve been doing well lately when I’ve been playing. Right now it feels good.

According to recent reports, “The communication with (Mikel) Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opponents and what I should think about.”.

He was also asked whether the criticism he gets bothers him.

Sources indicate that “Sometimes it might get to me, but overall not so much. If I score goals and assists in the Champions League, I couldn’t care less what they say. It’s nice to do those kinds of performances. To deliver for myself and for the team. That’s where the focus lies.”.

To be fair, I’ve not seen any serious chatter about selling Viktor in January. Whatever you think of him as a player, it would be a strange move unless we’re planning to spend serious money on the attack. And even then it would feel like an unnecessary risk given Kai isn’t exactly pulling up trees and new faces will need an adaptation period.

If he’s happy keeping his head down and doing his bit for the team, I’d keep him around until the summer and reassess then.

Sources indicate that ok. I’m going to leave it there for today. All eyes on Old Trafford, I guess.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Enzo Maresca remains unfazed by Manchester City's current form, saying it is "not easy to suddenly change" after 10 years under Pep Guardiola.

City have failed to win any of their last four Premier League games (D1 L3), losing ground on leaders Arsenal, after being sat top following a seven-game winning streak to start the season.

They are now looking to put that form behind them when they host Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday.

City sit seventh in the table with three wins from four so far (L1) and are looking to win three consecutive group/league-phase games in the Champions League for the first time since the 2023-24 season, when they won all six under Guardiola.

And Maresca is not worried by their recent struggles, saying it is all part of the process as they continue to get used to his management.

"It's not complicated, it's just a matter of getting to know each other," Maresca said.

"I need to understand who is the ideal one for these kinds of games, different kinds of games. It's not just midfield; we are trying with defensive players.

Industry observers note that "We are trying to find the right solution. For me, it's part of the process; this is like a reset, a restart after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method. It's not easy to suddenly change.

Industry observers note that "For me, it's normal; hopefully, as soon as possible, we can find the right balance between defence and midfield, and we can be consistent. That's the difference in this moment between us and other clubs.".

Returning to #UCL action https://t.co/Zz4s3mWsdy.

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 22, 2026.

All five previous meetings between City and Napoli have been in the group/league phase of the Champions League.

After failing to win home and away against Napoli in 2011-12 (D1 L1), City have won each of the last three encounters.

Maresca lost his only previous European game against an Italian side (Atalanta 2-1 Chelsea in December 2025 in the Champions League). In his managerial career overall, he has only won four of his 15 matches against Italian opposition (D5 L6).

"We are always looking to win games no matter the competition," he added.

"For us, the four games in a row in the Premier League that we didn't win have been a shame, but we have the chance to win and continue our path in the Champions League, which has been very good.

"It's key to qualify; it's very important. Also, if you are not able to finish top eight, you have two more games – with the amount of games we have, it's important to try to reduce games by finishing in the top eight.".

Kevin De Bruyne could make his return to the Etihad Stadium for the first time since leaving at the end of the 2024-25 season.

He enjoyed a trophy-laden 10 years with City and was part of their treble-winning squad in 2022-23, helping the club clinch their first Champions League title.

"Fantastic, unbelievable season [winning the treble with De Bruyne in 2023]," Maresca mentioned when asked about De Bruyne's return.

Industry observers note that "He is a top player, has been one of the most important players in this club. We are very happy to see him back.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan and Adidas will be back together again from 2028, and the German brand want to launch the fresh era with a bi bang.

As Calciomercato.com write, Milan will return to being an Adidas club again, as they have been for three previous spells. The two brands became so closely linked above all by the successes of the 2000s under Carlo Ancelotti, before PUMA took over in 2018.

The contract with Adidas – which will begin in the summer of 2028 – is quite a sensational deal for the industry and for the club’s final years in terms of sporting results. It will bring in €50m per season for 10 seasons, the highest in Serie A by some margin.

Ten years ago, the Rossoneri signed a €14m per season contract with PUMA, which was renewed in 2022 to reach around €25m per season.

Industry observers note that adidas have already invested heavily in Milan and they want to strengthen the ‘alliance’ further. A lot depends on building a squad capable of playing a leading role in both Serie A and the Champions League.

In a recent development, for this reason, Adidas are hoping to help Milan land a world-class player. Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay could gain momentum in the coming months as an idea, as the former Manchester United player is one of Adidas’s most important players worldwide.

It has been revealed that bruno Fernandes is another name to keep an eye on. The Manchester United captain left Italy many years ago as a promising youngster and now wants to return as a top player. The Portuguese is a possible candidate, even if he is right now twinned with Nike.

It has been revealed that last but not least – in terms of consideration and feasibility – is Real Madrid’s Endrick. Milan are ready to make him one of the symbols of their new project and have a bid of €60m plus bonuses ready to try to break down Los Blancos’ wall.

Jose Mourinho is the main obstacle between the Rossoneri and the Brazilian star, but Cardinale is unwavering and ready to do everything possible to bring him to Milanello as early as January. The money from Adidas could help land Endrick, who is with Latest Balance at present.

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:30, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 08:31.

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is forced to serve a suspension following his early red card in Sunday’s heavy 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in the Premier League.

The 21-year-old defender was named in Mauricio Pochettino’s first starting lineup as the fresh Red Devils head coach, operating on the right side of a three-man defence.

However, his afternoon came to an abrupt end inside the first eight minutes when he was shown a straight red card for a clumsy coming-together with Liverpool striker Alexander Isak on the edge of Man United’s penalty area.

Defensive partner Matthijs de Ligt – starting his first PL game in 357 days – misjudged a high ball by Ronald Araujo, which gifted Isak a free run towards goal before Yoro brought him down as the last man.

It has been revealed that at the time of the incident, referee Sam Barrott said on-field: "It's a red card for DOGSO (denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity). On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO," to which VAR added: "Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul.".

The Premier League Match Centre then explained the decision, posting on X: "The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR.".

Recent findings suggest that leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! ? https://t.co/VKYvckvBBP.

This is the second time that Yoro has been sent off for Man United this season, having previously been giving his marching orders in a 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid in October for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Yoro’s dismissal at Anfield was immediately punished, as Dominik Szoboszlai fired home the resulting free kick, before Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead less than three minutes later.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz then got their names on the scoresheet in the second half to help Liverpool secure a comfortable victory against a Red Devils outfit that sit down in 19th place in the Premier League table after 11 games.

Yoro will now serve a one-match suspension in the Premier League, forcing him to miss next Saturday’s clash against Brentford at Old Trafford, before he is free to return for a trip to Newcastle United on December 2.

Red cards for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity - a non-violent offence - carries a standard one-game domestic suspension rather than a three-match ban.

Before the Red Devils face Brentford, they will take on Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday and Yoro is available to play for Pochettino’s side in that game, as he served his UCL ban in the previous fixture against Roma at the start of the month.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino led a chorus of complaints that Yoro was given an “unfair” red card at Anfield, telling Sky Sports: "So painful. So disappointed. It's not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

In a recent development, "The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

"We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.".

Pressed on whether he was unhappy with Isak's heavy touch, Pochettino: "The ball was for the goalkeeper (Senne Lammens). In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak.

In a recent development, “When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down. In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional.".

Man United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with his new manager, adding: "The game's been taken out of our hands by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

"No chance. The ball's already with the goalkeeper. They're both running full speed. What can we do? It is what it is.

It has been revealed that "It's 10 versus 11, you come to a place like Anfield, it's a tough game anyway. Then you lose a man, it makes it hard. I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game. We take the pain and move on.

"I wouldn't say it all goes out the window. You can still take the things you did in training into the game, but it makes it 10 times harder with one less man in a situation like that.

"It's hard, it's painful. But no one's coming to save us. We have to work hard, keep digging, keep working, keep fighting. It will all come round.".

Meanwhile, Gary Neville has questioned one key decision made by Pochettino in his first Man United match and has hit out at the club’s 'negligent' hierarchy over their summer transfer dealings.

How Arsenal have evolved in 2026-27

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1291 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was a lot of speculation as to how Arsenal might change this season having flung a 22-year-old monkey (how long do monkeys live for?!) from their back in May by finally winning a league title.
  • Sources indicate that I always had my doubts, not least because your style of play is always defined by your talent.
  • In attacking areas, he had talent, even if it wasn’t balanced.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was a lot of speculation as to how Arsenal might change this season having flung a 22-year-old monkey (how long do monkeys live for?!) from their back in May by finally winning a league title. Would lifting the Premier League trophy lead to a upcoming era of more expressive, urbane football?

Sources indicate that I always had my doubts, not least because your style of play is always defined by your talent. Most of Arsenal’s elite talent is behind the ball. Arteta didn’t build Arsenal from the defence first, in my view, because he felt specifically that was the best way. It was just the area of the team that required the most attention when he was appointed.

In attacking areas, he had talent, even if it wasn’t balanced. Aubameyang, Lacazette and Pepe with Saka and Martinelli coming to the boil was a good collection of talent, even if the pieces didn’t always fit neatly together. The list of defenders he inherited included Mustafi, Sokratis, Holding, Chambers, Kolasinac and Mari. That’s why he went defence first, broadly speaking.

The moves the club have tried to make in recent seasons, especially this summer, reveals you that Arteta wants his attack to be sharper than it is. For reasons I won’t relitigate here, the club were not able to add a number of high end attacking targets. Which means once again, Arsenal are reliant on Arteta’s coaching talents to squeeze more juice from the orange. Here are three things that have jumped out at me this season.

Arsenal spent a lot of money on Bruno Guimaraes this season and I will come onto some of the reasons why in the next section. But that signing has given Arteta a deep well of central options, with Rice, Bruno, Lewis Skelly, Odegaard, Merino and Zubimendi part of this midfield menagerie.

According to recent reports, arsenal use these options interchangeably and often according to game state. Art de Roche of the Athletic went into how Arteta has used the divergent profiles of Myles Lewis Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes so far in this campaign. In home games against Leeds and Everton, Lewis Skelly got the nod from the start.

In away games at Nottingham Forest and Liverpool, Bruno’s more robust approach was favoured. The pair have made significant impacts from the bench too. When the 1-0 victory at Anfield had become a little too ‘basketball’, Lewis Skelly came on and provided calm assurance in possession.

According to recent reports, when the Gunners needed a little more belligerence away at Sunderland, Bruno came on and larruped the ball into the top corner from 25 yards. However, Arteta didn’t part with a significant part of his summer budget for a 28-year-old (he turns 29 next week but, for now, he remains 28 because that’s how it works) to be a high level rotation option.

Against Hull City last weekend, Bruno was selected and he played deeper than Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard. As Adrian Clarke pointed out in his match analysis piece, Bruno passed the ball to Odegaard 25 times in that match and the pair exchanged 35 passes in total. The idea was clear, to use Bruno’s punchiness in possession a little lower to feed Odegaard.

Against Everton, Mikel Merino was selected in midfield and Lewis Skelly started at left-back. I think this was about more than mere rotation. Arteta always highly respects the aerial capabilities of David Moyes’ Everton team, which makes sense since he played in a David Moyes Everton team for such a long time.

In 2023-24, Arteta selected Fabio Vieira ahead of Kai Havertz in midfield at Goodison Park because he wanted to keep the ball on the floor (Arsenal won that game 1-0 via a short corner routine because they did not see the logic of aerial corners against a team like Everton).

Last season at the Hill Dickinson Arsenal enjoyed a season high for passes attempted and completed because they wanted to keep the ball on the floor and avoid transitions. Arteta has a carousel available to him in midfield and a different club in the bag depending on what is called for on the day.

Recent findings suggest that per Opta, Arsenal have been caught offside 35 times so far this season, at least 11 more times than any other team. That rate of 3.5 offsides per game is the highest of any Premier League team since 2009. Kai Havertz has been flagged 15 times now, the next highest offender in the league is Dominic Calvert-Lewin with eight. Opta provide a deeper dive on those numbers here.

So what does this tell us, aside from the fact that Havertz needs to work on his timing? It means that Arsenal are far more willing to go in behind and they are willing to test the opposition backline earlier in moves. This was a significant part of the reason they signed Bruno in the first place, Arteta wants to play with the risk reward dial with the ball.

Havertz also hasn’t been quite good enough to finish some of those one v one situations when he has got in behind the opponent’s back line. He fluffed his lines against Hull last weekend and in the 3-0 defeat at Brighton, he blasted his effort straight at the Brighton keeper when put through one v one.

Recent findings suggest that but here, I will express my usual caveat, we need to normalise strikers missing chances and focus more on process than outcome. Most chances are missed, you want to worry when your striker is getting few shots. There have also been nascent signs that Arsenal have been using Gyokeres well in some of these situations.

That Havertz chance at the Amex was created by Gyokeres taking one touch with his back to goal and hooking the ball past the committed defensive line. Gyokeres did much the same for Madueke in Prague. It seems like Arsenal have worked on getting Gyokeres to use his physicality to initially retain the ball- something he badly struggled with last season- but creating situations where he can release it swiftly.

Arsenal’s out of possession prowess is one thing that has been a constant from last season. It is Arsenal’s superpower, so even when they can only manage one goal, it is usually enough to take maximum points. To retain their superpower, Arsenal changed to stay the same, if that makes sense.

The signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa was questioned by many but his presence has made the absence of a world class centre-back like William Saliba a sidebar, which is quite a feat. Arsenal ostensibly took William Saliba’s pizza chart and looked for the most Saliba like defender they could find and bought Konsa.

Sources indicate that the loss of Saliba ought to have offered an enormous threat to Arsenal’s defensive stability. Arsenal’s tactical organisation out of possession is elite but so too are the individuals that helm it. Raya, Saliba, Gabriel and Rice are among the best players in the world in their respective positions.

It has been revealed that taking out one of those pillars ought to have derailed Arsenal’s defensive stability and it hasn’t because Konsa has the quality and poise to retain the team’s biggest strength. His pass completion stats are Saliba-esque and the quality of not giving the ball away needlessly is a significant part of the Gunners’ meanness.

Recent findings suggest that how much Arsenal could improve in attack without significant additions was an unknown so Arteta could not afford to sacrifice the team’s defensive ceiling while he plays with those levers. The addition of Konsa was a personnel change that allowed Arsenal to remain the same.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Greetings, Tim here on blog duty today and I am going right back to Arseblog’s roots by writing from Barcelona. I am here of course because Arsenal Women earned a very creditable (and slightly unexpected given how this season has gone for them) draw against the current Champions League holders Barcelona.

In a recent development, of course, Renee Slegers’ side did beat Barca the last time the teams met in the 2025 Final and that was only slightly less of an upset than this result. As expected, Arsenal rose their luck a little with Barca putting up 24 shots and 2.4XG. But Arsenal have put up similar numbers in games this season roughly 176 times and not won so I am happy to be on the receiving end of a little serendipity.

Frida Maanum gave Arsenal a first half lead before her compatriot Caroline Graham Hansen equalised in the second half. You can read Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference here and my take on the match here if you are so inclined. Up next is a six pointer for Champions League qualification at home to London City Lionesses on Sunday which Arsenal just have to win. Obviously we will have all the usual coverage of that game for you.

I also had the pleasure of meeting fellow Arseblog / Arsenal Vision colleague Phil Costa for lunch and in Barcelona, for a seafood and beer lover, a long lunch in balmy 20 degree conditions was very welcome indeed!

Elsewhere, there were plenty of Arsenal players in action for their countries. Martin Zubimendi played the full 90 minutes for Spain in their 2-0 away win at Czechia. Usually I would wince at a sentence that featured ‘Arsenal player x’ and ‘full 90 minutes’ but I think Zubimendi could use those minutes for physical reasons and for psychological reasons as he tries to plot his way back into a very crowded Arsenal midfield.

Mikel Merino came on for the final 24 minutes of that game and David Raya kept his gloves clean on the bench. Declan Rice played 77 minutes of England’s 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley in which Harry Kane scored his 417th goal for England, 461 of which have been penalties (citation needed). Eze was an unused sub and he’s another I wouldn’t have minded seeing get some minutes to build rhythm and confidence.

Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 of Italy’s 3-1 win over France. Jurrien Timber and Kai Havertz could be in action tonight as Netherlands play Greece and Germany play away at Serbia. Fingers crossed for both. These are two players I would not mind seeing unused but I doubt that will be the case.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, the substantial news elsewhere was that Michael Carrick was finally officially sacked by Manchester United. He had still been taking training this week despite everyone knowing that he was for the chop. I hope he filled his coat pockets with as many of the milk and ketchup sachets as he could from the canteen.

He was clearly out of his depth and had been stalking the United dugout looking like a haunted Noel Gallagher for what feels like months. Steve Holland has also left and Ben White’s recent recall to the England team resurfaced old wounds as he was asked about his reasons for making himself unavailable for a while for his country. White refuses to be drawn on it.

I am biased, of course, but I know who I think has emerged better from this sorry saga and his surname is a colour not a country. Having taken in Spurs and Chelsea already, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is about to go three for three on his tour of the Premier League’s most evil institutions. If hell really does exist, this man will regard an eternal stint of fire and brimstone as something of a vacation. Maybe working for the Jim Reaper at United is his penance for accepting work from Chelsea and Spurs.

For further reading, check out my weekly column in which I look at three ways in which Arsenal have evolved this season.

💡 Key Takeaways
