  • Mikel Arteta revealed the injury sustained by Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is not feared to be too serious, but he will miss Tuesday's clash with Borussia Dortmund.
  • Arsenal return to Champions League action with a difficult test against the Bundesliga giants, and they must face Dortmund without their number one goalkeeper.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mikel Arteta revealed the injury sustained by Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is not feared to be too serious, but he will miss Tuesday's clash with Borussia Dortmund.

Arsenal return to Champions League action with a difficult test against the Bundesliga giants, and they must face Dortmund without their number one goalkeeper.

Raya was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Newcastle United after a coming together with William Osula in the penalty area.

In a recent development, the Spaniard, who has kept the joint-most clean sheets in the Premier League this season (seven), was seen clutching his shoulder as he left the field at St. James' Park on Saturday.

Raya has only conceded six goals in 19 Champions League games at the Emirates Stadium (0.32 per game).

Of goalkeepers with 10+ outings at a venue in the competition, only Jan Oblak at the Vicente Calderon has a lower goals conceded per game ratio (0.29 – four in 14 matches).

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had at that moment, and the first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging," Arteta told reporters of Raya's condition.

"He's not fit for [Dortmund] unfortunately, but it doesn't look too serious. [On Tuesday], we will be able to give you some more specific information.

"He does not need to have surgery, which was the worry as that would rule him out for months, so let's see.".

When asked about Raya's availability for this Sunday's clash with title rivals Manchester City, Arteta added: "[On Tuesday], we will have more tests, and then we will know.".

Champions League football in N5 https://t.co/6lKetPCaCW.

— Arsenal (@Arsenal) November 23, 2026.

Arteta remained tight-lipped on whether Kepa or Illan Meslier would start in Raya's place, but he made his feelings clear about Dortmund and their start to 2026-27.

Dortmund are two points clear at the Bundesliga summit after beating Borussia Monchengladbach 1-0 at the weekend, extending their unbeaten league run to 10 games (W7 D3).

Their 24 points from 10 matches are just one point fewer than their club record (25 points in 2010-11 and 2013-14), and they have made a strong start in Europe as well.

Kovac's side sit 12th in the 36-team standings on nine points, level with eight other teams in the Champions League, and Arteta is prepared for a testing encounter.

"I am very impressed with them, and you see their results so far, where they are in the Bundesliga and where they are in the Champions League," Arteta added.

"The way they are playing, the way they are dominating games. We had them here in pre-season, and they showed their quality and what they are capable of, so we are very aware of that, but we will play at home in front of our crowd and go and attack the game, that's for sure.".

Arsenal and Dortmund will meet for a ninth time in European competition, with each of the previous eight also being in group/league-phase matches in the Champions League (four Arsenal wins, three Dortmund wins – one draw).

The Gunners will be confident, though, given they are unbeaten in their last 19 Champions League games (W14 D5 – excluding penalty shoot-out defeats).

If they avoid defeat here, they will be just the third English team to go 20+ games without losing in the European Cup/Champions League, after Manchester United (25 – September 2007 – May 2009) and Man City (26 – September 2022 – October 2024).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026.
  • It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts.
  • “Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026. I’m in my hotel room in London, doing a few Arseblog bits on my laptop, and getting ready for the launch of the The 22 in the Major Red that night.

My phone rings. It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts. Typically I wouldn’t answer, but I think I know who it probably is. I’m right. It’s the Oncology department of the hospital I was admitted to a couple of weeks ago. They have news.

“We have the results of your biopsy.”.

“Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”.

“Great, we’ll see you then. Oh, and you should bring somebody with you. It’s a lot of information to take in.”.

As of this moment, I’m still not 100% on all the details. I had another scan yesterday, and I have a procedure scheduled for Tuesday which will give us more information. However, they’ve already laid out a proposal for three months of chemo, which is kind of why I’m writing this.

Recent findings suggest that my very, very strong instinct with any medical stuff is to keep it private. And I suppose if I was a guy who had a regular 9 to 5 and went to the office every day, I could do that. However, the privilege of my work is that it is very public facing. I do the stuff, you read the stuff and listen to the stuff, and you are part of my life in a very substantial way; in the same way – even if it it’s just for a few minutes each morning, or a couple of hours in your headphones – that I’m part of yours.

Which isn’t say I feel like I owe anyone an explanation, but this is my reality now, and for what’s likely to be an arduous road ahead for a while. Unfortunately, that makes it part of your reality too. I will say, I’m not going to document my ‘journey’. Fair play to anyone who does. Whatever you need to do to get through the challenges an illness presents, it’s just not really who I am. I don’t even do video on podcasts about football, so I’m not gonna start now for something like this!

But I do need the distraction of work, of Arsenal, of football and all its ludicrousness and drama, and this incredible community that has grown over the near 25 years of Arseblog’s existence. I’ve missed it this week, despite the fact it’s been such a difficult time in this household. We’ve gone through all the normal human reactions and emotions, and the whole thing was compounded by the fact I came back from London with the single worst stomach bug I’ve ever had in my life. To be honest, that felt a bit mean from the universe. Here, have a bit of this, and just to make you feel worse, you will require about twenty visits to the bathroom every day. It’s a bit like one of those days where every set of traffic lights you hit turns red as you approach, but the traffic lights also make your arse hurt. Fuck off!

So, I’m going to be around, and I’m gonna do my best to do what I normally do. I need as much normal as I can get, because right now too much isn’t. But there will be days when I’m not, or I can’t be, and I’m happy to let the lads pick up the slack as much as possible. To preempt many messages and thoughts, I know what the priority is, and I’m not going to push myself at the expense of my health or getting better. I have a vested interest in, you know, making a full recovery. I’m not going to risk doing anything that might conflict with that.

Recent findings suggest that but I also feel like the best way to navigate this is to not let it take over my life, or to define who I am. I’m still just an Irish bloke with a website about Arsenal first and foremost, and the last week or so has made me feel strangely protective of that. A dose of perspective is a really interesting thing, I know what the most vital thing is right now, but that can only succeed if I remain myself. I hope that makes sense.

Recent findings suggest that some lads kicking a ball around a football pitch is, in the grand scheme of things, not that notable. But hasn’t that always been the case? Football is so intrinsic to all of us, and we give so much of our time and energy to it, because we (well most of us) understand the absurdity of giving so much of ourselves to something that is completely out of our control. We can pretend otherwise, but that’s all part of the fun too. Lucky socks and lucky shirts and matchday routines. Our brain’s way of trying to make it feel like we have some influence, because we need that sliver of pretence, but in the end it’s about whether some millionaire at the back post can apply the finish.

Sources indicate that I suppose at least this shit waited until there was an Interlull. Thanks for that.

According to recent reports, I’m lucky because I have an amazing wife and daughter, and family and friends, who will be with me every step of the way. Their support thus far has been incredible, and I know I can count on it 100%. I’m going to listen to the doctors and the medical team and do whatever it is they ask of me. They seem to know what they’re on about, which is reassuring. Almost like they’re experts or something. We should listen to them.

I know as well that wider support from the Arseblog community will be forthcoming, and I just wanted to say in advance that I appreciate it hugely. I suspect that replying to every message is going to be beyond me, and in normal circumstances that would bother me greatly. I always try to respond to every email I get, even if it takes me a while, but in this instance I hope you’ll understand if I don’t or can’t.

So that’s where we are. I still don’t know where we’ll end up or how we’ll get there, but despite the fact I’m scared and worried, I’m also positive and determined. I could really do without this, to be quite honest, but it is what it is, and the only way through is forward. I’ll keep you in the loop as much as I feel I can, and in the meantime if Arsenal could make my day to day life as stress free as possible, I’d really appreciate that.

Someone have a word with Mikel and the lads.

AC Milan resume their Serie A campaign after the final international break on 2026 by welcoming Frosinone to San Siro.

In a recent development, ruben Amorim’s side are in need of a win to climb back into the top four after Como’s result on Saturday, while Roma and Lazio also picked up victories. They face a Frosinone team who will be full of confidence after an excellent start to their campaign, following promotion in 2025-26.

The latest team news suggests that Amorim will go with a 4-4-1-1 formation, though in his pre-match press conference he did not give too much away about his selection choices, especially in view of Thursday’s trip to Greece.

In a recent development, at the risk of sounding like a broken record, something simply has to click for Goncalo Ramos, and preferably soon. He has gone one month without a goal and his struggles to even generate shots followed him to Portugal on international duty. However, Frosinone are a side that score goals but also let them in too, so there should be spaces to exploit.

It will be an intriguing battle between the No.9 and Gabriele Calvani, while it could even be an audition of sorts for the centre-back. Milan have been linked with the Genoa loanee, who has made an impressive start to the campaign, so it will be an up-close look as he tries to pile the misery on Ramos.

In a recent development, with top scorer Antonio Raimondo out injured, Giorgi Kvernadze will be the main goal threat for the away side. The Georgian’s seven goal contributions are only bettered by the Italian striker, and he has started all 11 games under Alvini so far in Serie A.

It seems that Mario Gila will be tasked with stopping Kvernadze. The Spaniard spent the break at Milanello after not being called up by Spain again, and he should slot in as the right-sided defender again next to Koni De Winter.

Sources indicate that moving into midfield, there will be a fascinating contest between Adrien Rabiot and Giacomo Calo. It starts with a very obvious point of comparison: both are known for their goal scoring prowess, with the Frenchman already on five for the season and the Italian having racked up the same number.

Sources indicate that the pair are likely to face each other head-to-head too. Whereas Rabiot has usually played deeper like Calo, it seems that the head coach is thinking of moving him further forward to play behind Ramos, so he will see a lot of Calo and also Patrizio Masini.

Alvini is expected to give the nod to Aleksa Terzic at left-back, which is notable because the Serbian has only started one game so far in 2026-27, with his other four appearances all coming off the bench. He does like to get forward in transition though, and has a goal to his name.

Primarily, Terzic will be tasked with trying to limit Diego Moreira’s impact on the game. The Belgian – who scored for his national team for the first time in their rout of Italy – is expected to start on the right for the Rossoneri, and his seven goal contributions in seven games tell their own story.

Finally, we return to the middle of the park where Luka Modric and Romano Schmid will headline as series of interesting duels. Modric’s importance to Milan in all phases of the game have been written about at length, but particularly the build-up phase in games where his team are expected to dominate the ball.

The Croatian is the metronome for the Rossoneri just as the summer signing Schmid is for the Canarini. The Austrian has been playing mostly as an attacking midfielder, with two goals and four assists to his name, and starts in all 11 rounds thus far.

Mikel Arteta has clamped down on Arsenal stars' Fantasy Premier League (FPL) exploits after 'Tzatziki FC', Christos Tzolis' team, 'leaked' team news.

The Arsenal manager admitted he has 'taken measures' to ensure opponents are not given an advantage by his players' selections on the popular game.

Tzolis picked himself as captain of his FPL side prior to the Gunners' 1-0 victory over Liverpool, a clear indication that he would start after recently coming back from injury.

Arteta then caught wind of the situation and Tzolis removed all Arsenal players from his fantasy team for their next game against Hull.

X account FPL Focal identified 'Tzatziki FC' as the Greek winger's team and screenshots of his teams from both game weeks indicated how his picks changed.

According to recent reports, on Friday, speaking about this concern, Arteta stated: 'With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well. Constantly they are asking me about line-ups as well, because they want to know.

Christos Tzolis picked himself in Fantasy Premier League before starting the Liverpool game.

Tzolis' team, seen here before the Liverpool clash, is called 'Tzatziki FC' and was identified as his side by X account FPL Focal.

According to recent reports, 'It’s a topic, you know. These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it’s something new.

Industry observers note that 'We haven’t dealt with it [before] and we need to put latest things in place. Obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.'.

Arteta then confirmed that those measures had already been taken.

Tzolis is a known obsessive of the game, which puts him among 13 million other players who participate every year.

He even quipped after providing an assist against Coventry earlier in the season: 'I will take the three points', referring to the FPL score for doing so.

Chelsea had a similar problem this season, with their players indicating that Joao Pedro was out injured, removing the Brazilian from their FPL teams before his absence was confirmed by the club.

Teams are taking the matter seriously and are keen to ensure any possible advantage their opponents might have regarding team news is nipped in the bud.

Five years ago, Aston Villa stopped their players from participating in FPL after a number of them took Jack Grealish out of their line-ups, notifying eagle-eyed competitors that he was injured.

Mikel Arteta has cracked down on FPL use and 'taken measures' to ensure there are no leaks.

The potential impact of players joining the global GTA 6 mania is another concern for Arteta, with a number of top-flight players already sharing how gripped they will be by the new game.

Bryan Mbeumo posted the loading screen at midnight on Thursday, indicating that he was having a late-night gaming session just days before the Liverpool clash, while Alexander Isak has stated he will be hunkering down to play the game.

Declan Rice has previously spoken about how he often games into the early hours after matches when adrenaline is still coursing through him.

And his manager noted: 'We’ll try to find out how much exposure we have to these kinds of games and make sure it’s the right one to be able to perform and focus on what we have to do.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:50.
  • Tottenham Hotspur have received a major upgrade on the future of teenage starlet Luca Williams-Barnett.
  • The highly-rated academy graduate, who turned 18 at the start of October, made a notable impression on his full debut for Spurs in a 2-0 Premier League home win over Ipswich Town last weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 08:50.

Tottenham Hotspur have received a major upgrade on the future of teenage starlet Luca Williams-Barnett.

The highly-rated academy graduate, who turned 18 at the start of October, made a notable impression on his full debut for Spurs in a 2-0 Premier League home win over Ipswich Town last weekend.

Williams-Barnett opened the scoring with his first senior goal in the 15th minute, arriving at the back post to poke the ball home, before a blistering dribble that began from inside his own half helped him to set up Dominic Solanke shortly after half time.

Tottenham’s youngest scorer in the Premier League since Gareth Bale in 2007 received a standing ovation from the home crowd and also picked up the Man of the Match award.

After making his first-team debut as a 16-year-old last season, calls for the skilful winger to get more minutes have only grown louder over a challenging 12 months at Spurs.

Ensuring that Williams-Barnett commits his future to the club has also been high on the agenda, with the youngster having now entered the final 24 months of his current deal.

However, football.london reports that Williams-Barnett has agreed to sign a fresh long-term deal at Tottenham, seemingly cooling fears that he could leave to join a rival club.

The England Under-19 international has now featured four times in the senior Spurs side under head coach Roberto De Zerbi, who was full of praise for the “special” teenager after the win over Ipswich.

"Luca is a special player,” De Zerbi told reporters post-match. "I'm not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. He's lucky because he's playing in a top club with top teammates.

"I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was [James] Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be key.

Industry observers note that "The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom, and Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom.

"And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers.

"Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch.".

After revealed that Williams-Barnett prepared for the game on the team bus by watching YouTube videos of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, De Zerbi was asked whether the Spurs starlet could reach the same level as Barcelona and Spain sensation Yamal, who finished third in the 2026 Ballon d’Or rankings.

De Zerbi replied: "Yes, I think so, and one of the best things in my career… I've seen today in the bus from the training ground to the stadium, because he was very close with me, while we were coming in the stadium, he was watching on YouTube Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar.

Industry observers note that "I thought he was a special guy, because if one hour and thirty minutes before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. The football is magic, no?".

Williams-Barnett will hope to be rewarded with a second successive start when Tottenham travel to the Stadium of Light to face Sunderland in their next Premier League fixture on Sunday.

  • According to recent reports, lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could.
  • According to recent reports, where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

According to recent reports, lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless Upcoming Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

According to recent reports, where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

Industry observers note that and yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

It has been revealed that today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

According to recent reports, messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

You struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Industry observers note that messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

As a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose.

Sources indicate that to study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

Sources indicate that that alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

Como welcome AEK to the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Tuesday, hoping to maintain their strong start to their debut season in Europe's premier competition.

The Serie A side have won seven of their last eight games across all competitions, including a 9-1 win over Lens last time out in the Champions League, a result that puts them fourth in the 36-team table.

Fabregas' side also claimed a third consecutive Serie A home victory while also keeping a clean sheet for the first time since between October and November 1984 after beating Cagliari, but the Como boss was instead impressed by another managerial display.

Upon their return to Serie A, Frosinone are seventh in the standings, but were thumped 5-1 by Ruben Amorim's AC Milan.

However, Fabregas applauded Frosinone boss Alvini for his approach at San Siro, adding his tactics would be used as a template for their upcoming Champions League clash.

Industry observers note that "I'm taking the same approach as Alvini against Milan. I'm sticking to my ideas," Fabregas said via Gazzetta, as quoted by Football Italia.

"Of course, there are games we need to know how to manage in order to win, but we're not going to change all the good things we're doing.

"I'm proud of our last match against Cagliari, which featured so many fresh elements.

According to recent reports, "I still want to hear people say Alvini is a great coach. That is identity and courage, even if he lost 5-1. When you lose, you're rubbish; when you win, you're a genius.

"You need to keep things in perspective. Football is certainly changing, partly because referees are blowing their whistles less.

Recent findings suggest that "Fewer players are staying down because that tactic no longer works. It's a positive turning point for the Italian league, which is becoming one of the most entertaining in Europe.".

She swept into my law office with the determined gait of someone possessed by an idea.

Sources indicate that “Welcome,” I said, as she took the seat across my desk. “Any trouble getting here?”.

She shook her head. “No, except … They changed the rain schedule, so the taxidrone had to go the long way into town, but it’s fine.”.

According to recent reports, “Gotcha. I suppose introductions are in order. For my record-keeping, please indicate your name and IO registration. I’ll go first. My name is Leander Shah, I specialize in international treaty law, and I’m a biologically intelligent organism.”.

“I’m Joan Gorski,” she remarked. “I’m an artificially intelligent organism. I just turned 16. That gives me legal adult status under the UETO code.”.

I smiled. “Happy birthday, Joan. And you should know, I hold no bias against any human, regardless of intelligence source.” I nodded to the family photo on my desk. “My wife is an AIO. We’ve been happily married for 30 years and raised two AIO children, a boy and a girl. They’re grown now.”.

Joan glanced at the photo. “My mom is a BIO. She’s in the waiting room. She … didn’t want me to come. She thinks I’m just a stupid teen, being dramatic.”.

“So how can I help you? Your message was rather cryptic.”.

According to recent reports, she met my eyes, back straight, hands in her lap. “I’m going to sue the United Earth Treaty Organization’s Commission on Human Liberties for discrimination against AIOs.”.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

I leaned back in my chair. “The commission has guaranteed full human rights to all AIOs since 2105. How do you feel you’re still being discriminated against?”.

A hardness came into her expression. After a moment she blurted out: “I want the legal ability to commit murder.”.

This statement took me a few seconds to process.

“Joan,” I finally remarked, softly, “do you want to hurt people?”.

Sources indicate that “No! Of course not!” Tears came to her eyes. “God, you sound like Mom. I don’t want to hurt anybody. It’s not about that …” She took in a shaky breath. “I just want my choices to matter.”.

I shifted in my chair, pivoting to the window. Outside, taxidrones buzzed and the city towers glowed pink with the ivy bloom.

In a recent development, “Think about it, Mr Shah,” said Joan. “When a BIO commits murder, it’s recognized as a monstrous act of immorality. They’re punished, rightfully so. But any time someone is killed resulting from the actions of an AIO, then …” She left the thought dangling, waiting for me to finish it.

“Then the tragedy is blamed on a fault in the AIO’s software, hardware or something in their internal database of environmental impacts.”.

It has been revealed that “Exactly! And we aren’t punished, just reprogrammed. That’s wrong. It’s gross! It’s offensive!”.

I turned back to her. “Some people would call that progress, believing it’s actually better to —”.

According to recent reports, “I don’t want to be better! I want to be …!” She choked on a sob and abruptly stood, banging her knee against the desk and wincing.

Sources indicate that I held up a hand. “It’s all right, Joan.”.

“You just …” she sobbed, “… think I’m being … st-stupid …”.

It has been revealed that “No. I think you’re being human.”.

She laughed — one quick snort — then wiped at her eyes with the back of a sleeve. “Sorry.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Nothing to apologize for. As for your initiative to sue the commission, well … I actually agree with it.” This made such an enormous change come over her face that I swiftly added, “In principle. In reality, it would be very risky.”.

“We don’t have to win the case!”.

“No, that’s not what I mean. It would get press. It could … reignite the opposition to AIO rights as a whole. There are still a lot of BIOs out there who hate and fear the integration. They think it’s all part of some AI conspiracy to wipe them out. And now that AIOs outnumber BIOs two-to-one? They would interpret your lawsuit as evidence that AIOs can’t be trusted.”.

“I’m not saying your rights aren’t worth fighting for, but … perhaps there’s a lesser crime to consider, something less innately shocking than murder —”.

“No. It should be shocking. And I have to do it now, before I grow old and complacent and scared, like my mom. And if you won’t represent me, then I’ll find someone else.”.

It’ll be Ben White on the night

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid.
  • Industry observers note that obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England.
  • According to recent reports, holland was the one who sparked the glitch originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid. Ezri Konsa made it 2-0 with a close range header, Spain might wonder who was marking him (I think it was supposed to be Marc Cucurella) but the movement was really sharp. Then a couple of minute later, Ben White fired England into a 3-0 lead, with Cucurella also in close attendance.

Industry observers note that obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England. The worst sections of the media have fanned the flames against him, and it doesn’t take much to rile up those who are already of a jingoistic persuasion. As we’ve seen since seen with stories about Steve Holland being hugely unpopular at Man Utd, there’s a common denominator, and it’s not Ben White.

According to recent reports, holland was the one who sparked the glitch originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick. I also feel quite confident that even if there is a cohort who won’t forgive Ben White for the crime of Steve Holland being a dickhead, he probably won’t care too much. Look at the reactions of his teammates and manager to the goal, and that’s tells you plenty.

Industry observers note that he was also involved in a minor scuffle going off at half-time, which also seemed to involved Konsa and Martin Zubimendi, but I’m sure it was just heat of the moment stuff. Although Spain got two back after England went down to 10 men, they made the fatal mistake of starting Mikel Merino. How was he supposed to come off the bench and get a vital goal then? Silly Luis de la Fuenta, bloke’s a fraud.

According to recent reports, elsewhere over the weekend, Viktor Gyokeres scored twice for Sweden, both from the penalty spot. We just need more penalties. This is the key to unlocking him. Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 as Italy went down 4-1 to Belgium (ouch), Martin Odegaard played 90 as Norway beat Wales, and there are some more games to come this week with Germany facing Netherlands tonight (Kai v Timber), the Brazilians are in action in Singapore, and apparently Christos Tzolis is fit to play for Greece after having an MRI.

It has been revealed that maybe it’s my own recent experiences, but I don’t care for the idea he needs an MRI. I get it, it’s probably for his knee or hamstring or something, but it feels like if you need one of those to know if you’re fit, you’re probably not feeling 100% anyway. I guess this will be one Mikel Arteta will keep a close eye on tonight when Greece host Serbia and Tzolis inevitably starts. Ideally, these will be useful minutes for him, and help him deliver for us but you can’t help but worry considering he picked up an injury in the last Interlull.

Recent findings suggest that finally for today, it looks as if a Declan Rice contract extension is close. Speaking while on England duty, he said:.

Industry observers note that “A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon. I’m extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and teammates who put so much energy and effort into to me.

“I’m extremely lucky not to have to worry about that stuff, and it makes playing football far more easier.”.

This is, by any measure, a no-brainer. I don’t think there’s a club in the world that would turn him down if he were available, and his importance to Arsenal is just obvious. In a world when £100m+ transfers often struggle to provide value, this is one of the exceptions. If you went back to 2023 and had to do it all again, even if you added another £20m or £30m to the fee we paid West Ham, it would be worth it. It’s likely to be the kind of deal that sees him play out the rest of his prime years in red and white, and let’s hope there are more trophies along the way to accompany that.

According to recent reports, right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

Sources indicate that the pod should be out around around midday. Until then, have a good one – after which I’m gonna be off for a couple of days but the lads will keep things ticking here until I get back.

Divine Dowman does it again

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again.
  • According to recent reports, I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week.
  • It’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again. I suppose after 24 years of writing this blog, a few bad habits are bound to creep in….

According to recent reports, I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week. Fortunately, a lifetime of watching Arsenal has given me plenty of practice at making bad jokes when I don’t know what else to say.

It’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend. Bluesky, Reddit, X, Discord, Facebook, Patreon. Wherever I looked, there you were, sending love to Blogs. It was beautiful to see.

And to the handful of you who got in touch with me or people I know because you thought Friday’s revision was about my health, please hold that thought. I’m fine. Touch wood. There are, in fact, two Andrews at Arseblog, and I’m the other one.

Having been crowned the “World’s Youngest Boy” by James on yesterday’s Arsecast Extra, Max Dowman set yet another record last night, becoming England under-21s’ youngest scorer with the winner in a 3-2 victory over France in filthy conditions in Bristol.

I’d planned to watch from kick-off, but gave up when I realised the game wasn’t on any of the 5,000 channels I pay £150 a month for. Then I saw on social media that Ethan Nwaneri, playing as a number 10, had laid on a couple of goals. So I did the clever thing and googled it. Turns out I needed the official England app and an account. Eyes still rolling, I tried to set up a login, only to find out I already had one. Cue the password reset process, verification codes and me losing the will to live. Just let me watch some fucking children play football in the rain!

According to recent reports, by the time I got the stream, it was nearly half-time. At least that gave me a chance to catch up on Nwaneri’s two assists, both of which were Ozil-esque. First he drove down the left and slipped a neat ball inside for Mikey Moore, currently on loan at Cologne, to finish. Then came a teasing dink to the back post that Southampton’s Divin Mubama met first time. Given how little Nwaneri has played for Dortmund lately, it was a welcome reminder of what he can do.

It feels a bit silly to say Max, who was named player of the match, looked comfortable at this level when he’s already got a Premier League winners’ medal next to his GCSE textbooks, but he really did.

It has been revealed that watching him is like reading someone’s really nice handwriting. Even the everyday stuff looks lovely. A touch to bring the ball under control, a little turn, and suddenly the defender who was right up his arse is looking at the back of his shirt. I’ll never get tired of watching him do that.

As both sides made changes, I expected Lee Carsley to take him off. Instead, he played the full 90 and dug Arsenal teammate Tommy Setford out of a hole. The goalkeeper was at fault for the only goal in Friday’s defeat to Portugal and had another difficult night, spilling a cross into his own net. The rain hardly helped, and the 20-year-old has been doing well on loan at Stevenage, but it was a horrible one to concede.

According to recent reports, when Brest’s Giovani Versini whipped in an equaliser with five minutes left, it looked like England would have to settle for a draw, but Dowman’s tap-in settled it with a minute to spare. Who knows, Dowman and Nwaneri could be on the same pitch again next week when Dortmund visit the Emirates.

It has been revealed that elsewhere, Group 2 of League A of the UEFA Nations League (catchy naming scheme, lads) served up another bonkers evening. Jurrien Timber scored twice in the Netherlands’ 7-0 win over Christos Tzolis’ Greece on Friday, only for the Dutch to lose 5-0 to Kai Havertz’s Germany in Berlin. There were some lovely goals from the Germans – including two from Florian Wirtz – who are finding their feet under Jurgen Klopp. Timber and Havertz both came off midway through the second half, seemingly unscathed. Timber’s pride aside, anyway.

Tzolis, meanwhile, was cleared to play after an MRI scan and got through 88 minutes of Greece’s 1-0 win over Serbia. All three sides finished on 11 points, with Germany and the Netherlands going through on goal difference at Greece’s expense.

Tonight, Martin Odegaard’s Norway face Denmark, while Viktor Gyokeres will look to extend his record-breaking scoring run for Sweden away at Poland. Piero Hincapie’s Ecuador take on Bolivia, Massive Gabi and Bruno are in Singapore with Brazil, and Cristhian Mosquera and Marli Salmon are in action for Spain under-21s and England under-19s, respectively.

Sources indicate that closer to home, The Athletic ran two Arsenal contract stories in quick succession. James reports that Timber has agreed a newly introduced long-term deal, while David Ornstein notes Declan Rice’s extension will take him through to 2031. Arsenal already had the option to keep Rice until 2029, so the new deal effectively buys them two more years and gives him a sizeable pay rise for the next four and a half. If he keeps playing as he has been, I can’t imagine many Arsenal fans quibbling with that.

For what it’s worth, we’ve heard on the grapevine that David Raya’s new contract is all but done, too, which means the club are making good progress with the lads whose deals expire in 2028, a list that also includes Odegaard, Havertz, Mikel Merino and our two backup keepers.

There was an interesting discussion on Arsenal Vision’s ‘Friday Night Clive’ podcast about Arsenal elongating their “winning window” while having one eye on the next iteration of the team. If you hand expensive new contracts to players hurtling towards their thirties, you leave yourself financially exposed and potentially blocking pathways for up-and-coming talent. No doubt the club and manager are keenly aware of that. I just wonder how much you can expect the latter to focus on the faraway future when the dynasty he craves has to start in the here and now.

If this week has taught me anything, it’s that there’s something to be said for seizing the day. Admittedly, that’s easier when it’s Arsenal’s money I’m volunteering to spend.

If you’re about to part with some of your own (smooth segue, Allen) this year’s Arseblog Christmas Gift Guide is up.

I spent some of last week rounding up Arsenal bits and pieces I’d be happy to find under the tree. Mostly, I wanted to point you towards the independent makers, artists and writers producing stuff I like. In many cases, what I’ve picked is just a small sample of what they do, so have a nose around.

If you’ve got a recommendation of your own, pop the link in the form at the bottom and I’ll take a look.

Right, I’d better crack on with the day job. Lewis is on duty tomorrow and, all being well, Andrew M should be back here before the week is out.

A rather significant step was taken on Saturday, as Gerry Cardinale publicly declared AC Milan’s interest in signing Endrick.

La Gazzetta dello Sport have revealed that Cardinale spent six hours at Milanello yesterday, after four at Casa Milan. The owner fully immersed himself in the Milan world again: he spoke with his transfer team, with the team about the match against Frosinone, and with Ruben Amorim about both topics.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

While Cardinale did not confirm the imminent arrival of Markus Krösche – though he did admit to being in talks with him – his clear intention is to build a top-tier organisation. Cardinale’s goal is to lead Milan to a trophy – ideally the Scudetto – as early as this season.

To do this, he knows strengthening the squad in January is a necessity. One name stands out in his notebook: Endrick, the forward right now with Real Madrid whom Mourinho – for the time being – is unwilling to let go of.

Regarding a potential move for the 20-year-old, Cardinale confirmed that the club like him: “Endrick’s name keeps coming up in the market. Our project goes beyond any single player, but Endrick is one of the best in the world – if not the best – considering his age and position. I have enormous respect for him, and we’ll see what might be possible.”.

According to recent reports, in other words, the green light would need to be secured from Mourinho regarding his departure from Madrid. Milan know they can leverage the strong relationship between its owner and Roc Nation, the agency representing the Brazilian.

In a recent development, given the business already conducted between RedBird and Roc Nation, it is likely that the player would favour Milan over other potential destinations. Meanwhile, Tresoldi has also piqued Cardinale’s interest, though he offers a different profile than Endrick.

In a recent development, nicolo Tresoldi is also an option for the attack, but more significant progress has been made regarding the Brazilian. Bayern Munich are also watching the Club Brugge striker, with Harry Kane having undergone ankle surgery.

According to recent reports, in any case, Milan’s transfer activity will not be limited to a striker. Further arrivals will depend on the opportunities that arise during the winter window, with agents and intermediaries continually ringing the phone lines at Casa Milan.

There is a desire to bolster the defence, potentially with a central defender (possibly through the early return of Zachary Athekame, at the moment on loan at Lyon) and a left-sided player, should Pervis Estupiñán be sold.

All of this is in addition to the contract renewal for Rabiot, the next player set to be secured following the agreements reached with Strahinja Pavlović and Christian Pulišić. In short, there is a lot in the works.

Tech Report: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

💡 Key Takeaways

  • There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

Industry observers note that “We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, stated. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”.

Industry observers note that asked if he presently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”.

This was an Aston Villa team there for the taking after being gutted by their Premier League rivals and still waiting for fresh signings to be ready to play and gel.

But Arsenal made hard work of their victory and one senses there will be more games like this if Arteta has to rely on what he has already got until at least January.

Chelsea are showing they can score goals for fun having spent £117m on Rogers. Manchester City are strengthening their firepower with the signing of Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola has joined Liverpool. Arsenal have the defence and the midfield, but not necessarily the depth of quality in forward positions of their rivals.

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb.

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

According to recent reports, eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL.

Just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check indicated that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

The goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Industry observers note that defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

One of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his new club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

In a recent development, this is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

We lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

Sources indicate that to lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

I’m really happy. It’s a significant win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

Industry observers note that it was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

In a recent development, every substantial team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

It has been revealed that every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

[Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

Sources indicate that it was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

Sources indicate that I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

[Have you seen Chelsea?] I’ve seen them. [What do you think?] We’ll see on Sunday.

Jamie Carragher explains how Arsenal broke Aston Villa down for their winning goal 🔎 pic.twitter.com/CAI8zhznrJ.

Arsenal host Chelsea on Sunday at 4.30pm while Villa go to Hull City at 5.30pm on Saturday. It’s too early for a must-win game for Villa who highlighted some positive signs tonight but they could certainly do with one.

Arsenal win with a performance of efficiency and patience that emphasises their superiority when asked to grind out a result.

In a recent development, john McGinnis arguing the toss with the referee about his belief that he was fouled in the box in the dying seconds. It was outside the box and if Maatsen’s ‘tackle’ wasn’t a foul, neither was Gabriel’s.

Not sure the way of refereeing that lets a lot of calls go and waits for VAR is going to enhance the game.

Maatsen tackles Bruno Guimaraes in the Villa box with an ugly lunge in which he appears to scissor him, kicking his heel with one leg before knocking the ball away with the other but the referee deems it fair and VAR lets it pass, too.

It has been revealed that arsenal’s game management is working well as usual until Raya goes too long and the ball bounces through to Suzuki. But when he starts a counter-attack Alysson ends it with a dive and back come Arsenal.

Maatsen slides in late on Saka down the right, bypasses the ball and crashes into his shin. Yellow card.

Aston Villa probe but Arsenal hold them 30 yards from goal and when they do slide pass down the side of a defender for Buendia to chase, Bruno is ideally positioned to cover and make the block which he celebrates as if he were Leonardo Bonucci.

Eight minutes of stoppage time are signalled by the fourth official.

Suzuki races 15 yards outside his box to head a long pass away from Havertz to McGinn. Back come Arsenal after McGinn is squeezed off the ball but Wan-Bisska wins it back with a fine tackle. He is among the best one-on-one pure defenders in the league.

Zubimendi rattles Buendia’s bones in a crunching but legal tackle.

That was Rice’s last contribution as he limps off. He is probably OK but wise to withdraw him if he has had a twinge.

Maatsen drives down the left and cuts into the box. White leans into him, Rice guides him with a rigid left arm and the rampaging left-back loses his feet. Maatsen acknowledges Rice’s fine defending when he gets back up.

Quite a few outside observers questioned why Arsenal signed Konsa. This apparent injury to Mosquera is the reason. With Saliba out for months and Timber still struggling to regain his fitness, Mosquera was the only right-sided centre-back in the squad (unless they repurposed White, who is needed at right back).

Garnacho faces up Saka after being played down the left by Buendia but his cross is blocked by the goalscorer. Raya catches the resulting corner.

Sources indicate that mcGinn wipes out Merino from behind and is deservedly booked. Moments earlier Alysson was also booked for leaving one on Gabriel after the centre-half had cleared the ball, choosing not to put on the brakes and bodychecking him instead.

Unai Emery has just gone ballistic at substitute Alejandro Garnacho.

Emery clearly wasn’t happy with Garnacho not being ready to come on and let the Chelsea loanee know about it.

Garnacho → BarkleyWan-Bissaka → Cash.

And Mosquera cannot continue having overstretched so it’s a debut for the former Villa stalwart who is greeted warmly.

In a recent development, suzuki saves in a one-on-one with Havertz running through from 40 yards, waiting and refusing to go down and make things easy for Havertz, sticking up a right arm to block the shot. But he may have been offside which may mitiagte it in terms of not costing Arsenal anything but he really should have beaten the keeper.

Nice pass from Merino to set the hare running.

Barkley plays a diagonal pass across the turf out to Alysson on the right and he hares round Calafiori to cross from the byline but could not get the ball past Gabriel at the near post.

Abraham → JacksonAlysson → Hemmings.

Bruno → OdegaardMerino → Lewis-Skelly.

Now Maatsen goes flying but this time in the Arsenal box under a challenge from White that was a duplicate of the one 30 seconds before. ‘Premier League corrupt as f---,’ sing the Villa fans, ignoring the similarities between the two incidents. The defenders’ arms made contact with the attacking players but without the force to send them sprawling.

Havertz hits the deck in the Villa penalty area when challenged by Kamara as they fought for Odegaard’s scooped dink from the right.

Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino are stripped and ready to come on.

Once again, it’s Riccardo Calafiori who opens up the opposition’s defence with his off-the-ball running. He is the one player in this Arsenal team who makes genuinely unpredictable and unexpected movements.

McGinn’s combination with Jackson looks promising and the centre-forward invites him to bullock forward down the inside-right channel with a clever pass but the Villa captain is soon swamped by yellow shirts and the ball gets stuck beneath his feet.

Gary Neville makes the fair point that one of Arsenal’s most unheralded qualities is their patience. Their confidence in their rock-solid defence does not make them reckless but they are always confident of finding a way. They trust the method implicitly.

According to recent reports, aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1 (Saka) Mosquera has the ball 25 yards out, left of centre, he strokes it to Eze who angles a pass to Calafiori running between Cash and Lindelof. He makes it to the byline and cuts back a low cross that Saka and Maatsen both lunge at and the Arsenal winger gets there first to turn it in.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL.

Rice, Eze and Odegaard stand over it. Rive walks away and Odegaard approaches the ball with a semi-circular run-up. He whips it over the wall and about a foot wide of the left post. Suzuki was stranded but no matter.

It has been revealed that it was outside the box. Not all that sure it was a foul either. But Arsenal will have a free-kick.

Maatsen and Saka collide as they chase a Rice pass that Saka would never reach. Seemed to be outside the box.

It has been fairly dull fare so far as two systems and structures that cede little space clash.

Sources indicate that lindelof rises high to meet Rice;s dipping cross from the right as Havertz, on his shoulder, was poised to pounce. He heads it straight up and Suzuki leaps to catch it.

Sources indicate that now Barkley picks out a diagonal to send Jackson down the left. The centre-forward reaches the 18-yard line, cuts inside and works it over to McGinn who lofts a cross over Villa’s back-post runners and out of play.

Eze did his best work from the left last season. Villa start with Barkley scoop-chipping a pass from the middle out to the left, 40 yards upfield. Maatsen runs on to it and drives past White to ram a shot into the side-netting.

Eze replaces Tzolis for Arsenal.

Arsenal were too slow to move the ball forward in that first half, and too loose with it when they did get into promising positions. There’s a lack of urgency in their passing. I wonder if we’ll see Bruno Guimarães soon… one of the reasons they signed him was to add more quick forward passing to their play.

In a recent development, signs of encouragement for Villa without creating much while Arsenal have been stymied so far by Villa’s neutering of Tzolis and the left wing. Arsenal’s right-sided trio – White, Odegaard and Saka – look the most likely to create something.

Sources indicate that only a minute of added time to be played. Arsenal still lacking a spark, largely because there’s a lack of precision in their forward, line-breaking passing.

Recent findings suggest that villa will be very happy with this half. Much more like their old selves in terms of structure and organisation.

Sources indicate that calafiori’s throw to Gabriel is picked off by Jackson down the right and he dribbles down the right. He is forced to slow down to wait for a midfield runner. When Hemmings catches up, so have three Arsenal defenders and though Jackson bends in a low, cross to the edge of the six-yard box it is about 18 inches away from Hemmings’ reach.

Recent findings suggest that calafiori goes down in the Villa box when Pau Torres uses his arm to lever him away as they tracked the flight of a cross. The referee sees nothing wring in it and neither does VAR.

Sources indicate that gillett takes an age to stop the play when Cash uses his body to shove Tzolis over after the winger had played a pass. Cash obviously thinks he has rattled the fresh signing and is keen to rough him up some more. The ref does award a free-kick but only after that daft delay.

Industry observers note that tzolis loses the ball on the edge of the Villa penalty area, tackled by McGinn. The captain slots a straight pass up to Buendia who tries to bend a pass into Jackson’s stride as he sprinted down the inside right channel but Gabriel read the trajectory and got there first.

In a recent development, suzuki picks out McGinn with a long pass. He feeds it to Buendia who gives Hemmings a chance to chase it down the left. Arsenal shuffle over in defence so he doubles back and returns the ball to Buendia. The No 10 whips over a dipping cross looking for Barkley and Jackson but Calafiori and Raya make sure the goalkeeper wins it.

According to recent reports, we’ve not seen much from Christos Tzolis on Arsenal’s left wing so far. He’s been excellent since joining the club this summer but he’s hardly seen the ball in this opening half an hour and he’s just been booked after losing a battle with Matty Cash.

Arsenal free-kick 30 yards out, left of centre, for a foul on Lewis-Skelly who was artfully shielding the ball. Odegaard chips to the right post but Havertz heads it back across the box rather than going for goal and Villa clear.

According to recent reports, cash gets the better of Tzolis again in the tackle and then Suzuki sprays a perfect 60-yard pass out to Hemmings that Gary Neville, likening it to something Ederson was capable of delivering for Man City, one of the best goalkeeper passes he has ever seen. Tzolis was booked for stopping Cash running off with the ball.

Maatsen, who could never dislodge Digne for long, has a chance now to make the position his won. He strides down the left, exploiting Rice’s positioning error but his right-foot isn’t half as good as his left and his bending effort is scuffed far too straight and easily cleared.

According to recent reports, saka drives down the right after a neat Odegaard, Saka, White triangle. Pau Torres races over to toe the ball behind for a corner. Saka takes and Rice flicks it on at the near post and Suzuki tips it over. No corner, though, as Gabriel had rag-dolled McGinn at the back post after the Villa captain had backed in to him and tried to stop him making a run into the middle.

“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that.” Villa fans poke the wound.

Arsenal are finding it difficult to play through the middle of the pitch but have found Saka in space on the right wing on a few occasions already. Villa are congesting the central areas, where Odegaard does his best work.

Calafiori picks off Kamara’s pass looking, for the third or fourth time, to play someone, usually Jackson, in behind the left-back. A minute later Calafiori challenges McGinn for a bouncing, loose ball and stoops to use his head. colliding with McGinn’s boot. Was the head low or the boot high? Arsenal think the latter but the ref sides, rightly, with McGinn.

According to recent reports, arsenal corner on the left. The threat inherent every time Rice is in a quadrant diminished on this occasion because Mosquera barged Cash just after Rice struck the ball. Free-kick to Villa.

Timber may be preferred by Arteta at right-back but Saka prefers White. The two have a well-grooved partnership in tersm of who underlaps and who overlaps. They never seem to get in each other’s way.

Bukayo Saka does seem to be getting a lot of time and space on the right flank.

It’s looking a risky tactic by Villa at the moment as the England international is being invited to cut in towards the penalty area.

Havertz is played down the inside-right channel in the penalty area by a cute Odegaard pass bur he blazes his shot across goal and wide of the left post. A replay shows he was offside but even so it was a lazy finish.

Kamara grabs Tzolis round the waist from behind and when the winger hits the deck, rounds him and passus to Buendia who crashes a right-foot diagonal shot on to the bar from 20 yards. The ref did not see it as a foul despite Arsenal’s protestations but had it gone in it would have given VAR a dilemma.

Worth keeping an eye on Aston Villa midfielder George Hemmings tonight.

He is only a teenager and has emerged from Villa’s academy, but Unai Emery is already a huge fan.

Hemmings produced a highly promising performance in the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Suzuki misjudges the flight of Rice’s typically menacing corner and flaps at it but his defenders and an offside flag leave him without egg on his face.

Recent findings suggest that mcGinn stops Calafiori down the left then gives the ball straight to Tzolis. The Greece winger opens his body and passes to Lewis-Skelly who shoots with his right foot from the left of the 18-yard line. Cash slides in to block the shot and it loops over the bar for a corner.

Hemmings uses his strength to hold off Ben White and shift the ball inside to McGinn who wraps his left instep around a shot and wafts it into building site behind Raya’s goal.

Industry observers note that ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are in the directors’ box watching the game. Villa don’t look like a hastily assembled team.

According to recent reports, suzuki knocks the ball long with his left foot, looking for Jackson but the ball spins away from him to Raya who boots it back upfield. McGinn pounces on it, turns past Rice and plays Cash in down the right. He crosses towards the near post and Mosquera hooks it clear.

Industry observers note that arsenal kick off with Odegaard spinning and trying to play Saka in down the right as they defend the empty North Stand end. The ball skids off the turf and Saka can’t trap it. The ball goes out for a Villa throw-in.

Who dies in the summer and played for both clubs.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal are in fact in yellow and navy. My mistake.

Villa in claret and blue with a twist, the shorts are blue for the first time since, I think 2001. Arsenal are in yellow and black. Leeds, like Arsenal, have traditionally worn yellow and blue as their away strip but have been shunted into yellow and black as well by Adidas this season.

There are a few guys standing in the North Stand with hard hats on, and it appears they are on ball retrieval duty.

They will be on red alert for any wayward shots that land in the empty stand.

Warm reception for Ezri Konsa from Villa’s fans as he walked back to the tunnel with Arsenal’s substitutes.

Konsa joined Arsenal last week for £51m, ending a spell of seven years at Villa Park.

Wonder if the likes of Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez will get a similar reception when they return here with Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that aston Villa  Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Barkley; McGinn, Buendía, Hemmings; Jackson. Substitutes  Bizot, Mings, Ruggeri, Garnacho, Abraham, Bogarde, Wan-Bissaka, Edward, Lynch.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal  Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz. Substitutes  Arrizabalaga, Hincapié, Eze, Gyokeres, Konsa, Madueke, Merino, Zubimendi, Guimaraes.

Referee  Jarred Gillett (Australia).

Zion Suzuki is one of two debuts for Aston Villa tonight and there is a genuine buzz of excitement around the Japan international.

Suzuki was signed from Parma for £30m as the replacement for Emiliano Martinez and arrives with a stellar reputation.

He’s got big boots – and gloves – to fill, but Unai Emery is convinced he will become a future star at Villa Park.

The other debutant is record £65m signing Nicolas Jackson, who joined last week from Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that good evening. Yes, the first match was not as planned but we must keep going forward. Today we are playing our first home match and I am looking forward. We need to try as soon as possible to get our best individuals fit for a good performance. And today is a good match for us. Ir is difficult but always with our supporters here we feel comfortable and confident. Hopefully we can transmit our positive energy to our supporters.

We lost the first game but it is not a [team full of rookies]. We have experienced players. They play with energy and know how we want to play. We have to adapt with Suzuki but we have confidence [in him]. Jackson, the striker, and other players, George Hemmings, he is young but played fantastically in pre-season. He knows how we want to play.

According to recent reports, today is a challenge but I’m really looking forward to how the players will respond collectively, individually. We know we are changing things but no excuses. We have to perform today, we have to try to adapt the upcoming players, to build our team to get their best today.

In a recent development, I am positive and I am optimistic. The players are ready.

Aston Villa are in a transition period and rebuilding on and off the field.

Unai Emery’s 2.0 have been under construction all summer and there could be 10 new signings in by tomorrow morning.

Villa have of course lost six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final, with Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Emiliano Martinez and Lucas Digne all departing this summer.

The North Stand at Villa Park, which faces the iconic Holte End, is also under renovation and closed down for tonight’s game.

It could be a bit quieter tonight but there is still a mood of optimism among Villa fans, despite such a summer of change.

We have had a real block of training sessions to work on things and prepare for this game in the right way.

We will have time to make changes throughout the game [on why he has picked an unchanged team]. They did really well [against Coventry] and for the game we expect [tonight] they have the right qualities to hurt them and that’s how we start.

Recent findings suggest that they have that [upheaval in personnel] but they have been with Unai for a long time, they are a super well-coached team and we know how tough it is always to come here. We are very conscious of that but also very ambitious.

That’s the way we want to play [with aggression] constantly from the first minute, to suffocate the opponent and be better than them.

[Does it being your 250th Arsenal Premier League game add something special to it?] Just to win [makes it special].

She wore… she wore… she wore a yellow ribbon ….

Two changes – Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson make debuts. Joao Gomes misses the match as the first of his three-game suspension and Marco Bizot drops to the bench.
